questions.text: What is the primary mechanism of dividend reinvestment in a long-term strategy?
options: Using distributed profits to purchase additional shares without spending new personal cash
Selling existing shares when prices peak to generate cash dividends
Borrowing funds to increase total share count during market drops
Switching all portfolio assets into cash to prevent short-term losses
questions.explanation: Reinvesting dividends turns cash distributions into additional shares without requiring extra cash outlay.

questions.text: How does dollar-cost averaging automatically respond to fluctuating share prices?
options: It buys an equal number of shares at every scheduled purchase date
It purchases fewer shares when prices are lower and more shares when prices are higher
It purchases more shares when prices are lower and fewer shares when prices are higher
It pauses all purchases automatically whenever share prices decline
questions.explanation: Investing a fixed amount means you acquire more shares when prices are low and fewer shares when prices are high.

questions.text: True or false: Dollar-cost averaging completely removes investment risk and guarantees a lower average purchase price.
questions.explanation: Dollar-cost averaging does not remove investment risk or guarantee a lower purchase price.

questions.text: True or false: A written investment plan helps investors avoid emotional decision-making by establishing clear guidelines before market volatility occurs.
questions.explanation: A written policy statement acts as an anchor that removes guesswork and prevents panic during market fluctuations.
